Role in the stack: Turn each incoming document into plain text. One format reader exists per supported format.
Why this choice: We decided to reuse the readers that run today. New readers would repeat what the current ones already do.
Infrastructure: Container jobs, started when a file arrives
Notes: Row I2 consumes the reader output.

Role in the stack: Turn reader output into one canonical form, fixing character encoding, spacing, and token boundaries.
Why this choice: We decided to normalize once. Every later component then reads one form instead of handling each variation itself.
Infrastructure: Container jobs, run after row I1

Role in the stack: Copy document properties into index fields: author, date, and source system.
Why this choice: We decided to adapt the existing extractor. The mechanism exists, and this system supplies only the field mapping.
Infrastructure: Container jobs, run after row I2

Role in the stack: Map each term to the documents that contain it. The core lookup structure for search.
Why this choice: We decided to keep the inverted index. Its lookup cost per term stays flat as the collection grows, and a full scan's cost does not (row X1).

Role in the stack: Map equivalent terms, so a search for one form also finds the others.
Why this choice: We decided to adapt the existing table. Wording differs across source systems, and the table absorbs that difference once, at index time.
Notes: Table entries are versioned. Row Q1 reads the active version.

Role in the stack: Accept a search request, expand it through the synonym table, and read the index.
Why this choice: We decided that one service owns query meaning. Every caller then gets the same answer for the same request.

Role in the stack: Order the matching documents before the query service returns them.
Why this choice: We propose ordering by term frequency and by how recent a document is. Nothing has evaluated the proposal against sample searches.
Infrastructure: None. Row Q1 supplies the runtime.
Notes: The ranking rule is proposed, not selected. Row Q1 returns matches in index order until a rule is selected.

Role in the stack: Hold the source documents and the index snapshots.
Why this choice: We decided to reuse the object storage the team already operates. No further storage system is needed.
Infrastructure: Managed object storage, with rules that expire old snapshots

Role in the stack: Collect job outcomes, search response time, and index freshness.
Why this choice: We decided to reuse the existing monitoring. It already collects all three signals, so no further tooling is needed.
Infrastructure: The existing metrics and logging pipeline
Notes: None. The row states coverage and asks for no action.

Role in the stack: Read every document on every search, instead of consulting an index.
Why this choice: We decided against a full scan. Its cost rises with the size of the collection, and search response time has a fixed budget.
Where it runs: Not applicable. The approach was not taken, so nothing runs it.
Infrastructure: Not applicable. The approach was not taken, so nothing is deployed.
Notes: Row N1 is the approach taken instead.

Role in the stack: Send the documents to an outside search provider, and search them there.
Why this choice: We decided against an outside provider. The documents may not leave the operating environment, and the index has to stay open to inspection.
Where it runs: Not applicable. The approach was not taken, so nothing runs it.
Infrastructure: Not applicable. The approach was not taken, so nothing is deployed.
